generated_examples.rule: Each source becomes one research-only example. No parcel CIL liability, S106 compliance, viability acceptance, infrastructure delivery or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck charging schedule, agreement and contribution evidence against exact permission date, floorspace, relief/exemption, indexation, legal agreement and site status. Authority-level rates and reports remain separate from parcel liability.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck receipts, allocations, transfers and future priorities against physical infrastructure delivery. Allocated/spent/transferred does not automatically mean the target site's mitigation is complete.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck end dates, supersession, pending decisions, draft schedules, historic IFS periods and agreement triggers. Newer operative legal/planning evidence takes precedence before promotion.

extra_examples.fact: The national developer-agreement dataset has 78 providers and mixed authoritative/MHCLG-created provenance.
extra_examples.gate: No national record cannot be interpreted as no S106/CIL/S278 agreement; check the exact LPA register.

extra_examples.fact: Section 106, CIL and Section 278 are controlled agreement types.
extra_examples.gate: A type definition creates no parcel liability or obligation by itself.

extra_examples.fact: The authoritative record links an S106 to a specific planning application.
extra_examples.gate: Agreement existence is separate from trigger, payment, discharge and compliance states.

extra_examples.fact: The developer agreement is linked to an outline planning application.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer reserved matters, commencement or delivery from the outline-linked agreement.

extra_examples.fact: The developer-agreement record has an end date of 16 February 2024.
extra_examples.gate: Reject it as current live obligation evidence unless superseding authoritative material is found.

extra_examples.fact: The agreement record begins in 1992.
extra_examples.gate: Historic age alone requires current planning-register/title/obligation verification before use.

extra_examples.fact: CIL liability depends on chargeable development, calculation rules, relief/exemption, collection and timing.
extra_examples.gate: Headline rate multiplied by rough area is not an accepted liability calculation.

extra_examples.fact: CIL collection operates through statutory notices and commencement-related rules.
extra_examples.gate: Planning permission date and development commencement/payment states must remain separate.

extra_examples.fact: Viability material is evidence considered in planning decision making.
extra_examples.gate: An applicant appraisal is not an agreed reduction in affordable housing or contributions until the decision maker accepts the position.

extra_examples.fact: Planning obligations must meet necessity, direct relationship and scale/kind tests.
extra_examples.gate: The policy tests do not specify the amount or content of an individual site's agreement.

extra_examples.fact: MCIL rates are indexed and the applicable annual summary depends on the permission year.
extra_examples.gate: Use exact permission date and chargeable floorspace; do not apply a static historic rate.

extra_examples.fact: CIL charging functions are affected by the OSDC planning-function transition process.
extra_examples.gate: Resolve the operative charging authority on the relevant permission date before calculating liability.

extra_examples.fact: The IFS reports financial and non-financial developer contributions and infrastructure funding intentions.
extra_examples.gate: Authority allocation is not evidence a target development's mitigation has been delivered.

extra_examples.fact: Croydon publishes approved S106 expenditure through June 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Approved expenditure elsewhere in the borough does not establish a target parcel's obligations or infrastructure benefit.

extra_examples.ref: Draft CIL review versus operative schedule
extra_examples.fact: Croydon is publishing review/examination material for a revised charging schedule.
extra_examples.gate: Keep draft/review rates separate from the currently operative adopted schedule until effective.

extra_examples.fact: Cambridge's 2026 process concerns a draft CIL schedule and consultation/decision steps.
extra_examples.gate: Do not calculate parcel CIL from a draft consultation schedule without final adoption/effective-date evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Leeds provides application-level CIL compliance, amount due/paid and discharge status checking.
extra_examples.gate: Use exact application status rather than authority-wide fund percentages for a parcel.

extra_examples.fact: The Leeds IFS notes developer-contribution data represents estimates at a point in time and can change.
extra_examples.gate: Revalidate current agreement/payment records before relying on historical IFS totals.

extra_examples.ref: Oxford S106 trigger versus payment gate
extra_examples.fact: Oxford's IFS lists agreement trigger information for named contributions.
extra_examples.gate: A trigger clause does not prove the trigger occurred or payment was made.

extra_examples.ref: Oxford future CIL programme revision gate
extra_examples.fact: Oxford states future CIL programme allocations may change during budget setting.
extra_examples.gate: Future allocation tables are not immutable infrastructure delivery commitments.

extra_examples.fact: Oxford has an adopted August 2025 charging schedule.
extra_examples.gate: Exact use, floorspace, permission year, indexation and relief/exemption remain required for site liability.

extra_examples.fact: The Bristol page currently marks the 2024/25 S106 report as coming soon while publishing other IFS components.
extra_examples.gate: Missing publication must not be converted into zero S106 activity.

extra_examples.ref: Bristol held money versus project delivery
extra_examples.fact: Bristol reports S106 money received/held and allocation processes.
extra_examples.gate: Held or allocated cash does not prove physical infrastructure is built or a target site's obligation is satisfied.

extra_examples.fact: Merton points users to the exact planning application record to view individual S106 agreements.
extra_examples.gate: Use the linked case and deed, not borough-level summaries, to assess a parcel.

extra_examples.ref: Milton Keynes fees versus liability gate
extra_examples.fact: Milton Keynes publishes 2026/27 planning-obligation fees and monitoring processes.
extra_examples.gate: Administrative/monitoring fees are not the complete development contribution liability.

extra_examples.fact: Reading's IFS reports past contribution flows and highlights future spend.
extra_examples.gate: Highlighted future spend is not a binding promise to deliver infrastructure for a specific development.

extra_examples.fact: Reading lists CIL, S106 and affordable-housing policy documents together in the examination evidence library.
extra_examples.gate: Document existence does not identify which policy requirement applies to a target proposal without exact use/scale/date analysis.

extra_examples.fact: The IFS identifies infrastructure types the council plans or may fund.
extra_examples.gate: 'Plans or may fund' is not guaranteed project delivery or site-specific mitigation.

extra_examples.fact: On 24 July 2026 the 2024/25 IFS decision is shown as for determination with a due date of 27 July 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not report the statement as approved before an authoritative decision record confirms approval.

extra_examples.fact: The 2023/24 IFS was approved in December 2024.
extra_examples.gate: Use it as historical reporting only once a newer 2024/25 statement becomes authoritative.

extra_examples.fact: Dover reports S106 receipts by infrastructure category for 2024/25.
extra_examples.gate: Receipt totals cannot identify whether a named parcel still owes, has discharged or has no relevant contribution.

extra_examples.fact: Dover defines spend to include internal and external transfers from the S106 account.
extra_examples.gate: Accounting transfer must not be equated with physical infrastructure completion.

extra_examples.ref: Dover future priority versus guaranteed scheme
extra_examples.fact: The IFS identifies future infrastructure and affordable-housing priorities.
extra_examples.gate: Priority status is not a funded, consented or delivered project guarantee for a target parcel.

extra_examples.fact: Arun warns its pre-April-2019 S106 transaction data can be limited.
extra_examples.gate: No transaction hit for an older agreement cannot be interpreted as no obligation or no payment.

extra_examples.fact: Southampton reports local, strategic and administration portions of CIL receipts.
extra_examples.gate: Fund-share percentages do not determine the exact liability or infrastructure benefit of one development.

extra_examples.ref: MCIL1 to MCIL2 supersession date gate
extra_examples.fact: MCIL2 superseded MCIL1 for relevant permissions from 1 April 2019 and the older Crossrail S106 SPG ceased for later permissions.
extra_examples.gate: Use permission date to select the operative regime and never stack superseded contribution rules.
